primary_sources.paper: Repair or Resample? Rethinking Failure Debugging in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
observed: 54 initially successful executions were rerun three times under the same runtime configuration; 85/162 rerun attempts failed and 39/54 source-success cases regressed at least once.

On 536 SymFail source failures, pass rates were Last-Node 1.31% pass@1, Random-Node 3.73% pass@1, Critic-Agent 3.73% pass@3, Self-Reflection 4.29% pass@3, Unguided Full Rerun 6.90% pass@3, Suspicious-Node 20.15% pass@1.
The authors explicitly state symptom-based target selection and repair guidance are changed jointly, so the 20.15% result cannot be attributed to either component alone.
The paper reports SymTrace/SymFail release in text, but the arXiv article metadata did not expose a direct first-party GitHub link during this audit.

primary_sources.paper: ToolMisuseBench: An Offline Deterministic Benchmark for Tool Misuse and Recovery in Agentic Systems
observed: Public-test overall metrics: heuristic success/recovery/calls 0.250/0.000/2.95; schema-repair 0.250/0.250/3.25; policy-aware 0.250/0.250/3.25.

Fault-specific recovery: timeout 0.502 for schema/policy versus 0 for heuristic; schema drift 0.497 for schema/policy versus 0 for heuristic; released authorization and rate-limit success are 0 for all three baselines.
Paper explicitly limits policy-aware baseline to a lightweight heuristic and says simulator evidence complements rather than replaces live-system evaluation.
Paper links official repo akgitrepos/toolmisusebench and states same reproducible pipeline produces reported results.

primary_sources.observed: Current official repository exposes deterministic generation/evaluation, fixed-seed fault injection, heuristic/schema_repair/policy_aware baselines, and a reproduce-paper command. Exact paper table numbers were not independently rerun in this tool environment.

material_findings.claim: Broad full rerun has a substantial success-to-failure disruption channel in the reported MAS setting.
material_findings.scope: The 85/162 and 39/54 figures are directly reported for 54 initially successful SymTrace executions rerun three times under the same runtime configuration. This is not a universal rerun failure rate and does not establish the mechanism of each regression.

material_findings.claim: Suspicious-Node provides much higher descriptive repair yield than the task-level baselines.
material_findings.scope: 20.15% is pass@1 whereas task-level methods are pass@3. This actually rules out a larger attempt count as the explanation for Suspicious-Node's higher pass rate, but it is not a compute-matched component ablation. Target selection plus symptom-conditioned repair guidance are a joint intervention.

material_findings.claim: Recovery utility is fault-class dependent in ToolMisuseBench.
material_findings.scope: Schema/timeout recovery improves under the two repair baselines while released authorization/rate-limit subsets remain at zero success. This supports classification before retry budget in this deterministic synthetic benchmark; it does not show that authorization faults are intrinsically unrecoverable or that stronger policy-aware planning would fail.

material_findings.claim: Aggregate success alone can hide fault-local recovery improvements.
material_findings.scope: All three baselines remain at 0.250 overall success even though schema/timeout recovery differs sharply. This is benchmark/profile specific and should not be generalized to arbitrary task mixtures.

downstream_implication: Long-horizon recovery evaluation should keep rescue and disruption as separate paired outcomes and condition recovery spending on fault/reachability class. Do not infer component-level causality for Suspicious-Node or universal unrecoverability from the released ToolMisuseBench baselines.
exact_next_action: Rotate to sealed C24 failure_evidence. Prefer a claim whose primary artifact can distinguish measured failure from mechanism attribution or whose current evidence status can change admission.
